Q_001,How do I get help for food like SNAP or other places?,"## You can get food help right now
- **Call 2‑1‑1** – a free state helpline that will connect you to local food banks, pantries, and emergency shelter.
- **Visit a nearby food pantry** – many counties list pantry locations on the CDSS “Find Food Banks” page.
- **If you’re in crisis** (no food at home, at risk of homelessness), call the **CalFresh Benefits Helpline 1‑877‑847‑3663** or dial **211** for immediate referrals.

Q_002,Can I recieve multiple types of assistance at the same time?,"## You Can Receive More Than One Benefit at the Same Time
**Yes – many California assistance programs allow you to receive several types of help together.**

The key is to apply for every program you qualify for and to tell each agency about the other benefits you’re getting. That way they can determine the right payment amount and make sure you stay in compliance.

column1: ### How to Apply for Multiple Programs
1. **Gather basic documents** (you’ll need most of these for every program).
- Photo ID (driver’s license, state ID, or passport)
- Proof of California residency (lease, utility bill, or mail)
- Social Security number (or ITIN)
- Recent pay stubs or proof of unemployment (if any)
- Bank statements (to show assets, usually <$1,000 personal property)
- Benefit letters or award notices if you already receive another program (e.g., CalFresh card, SSI award letter)
2. **Apply one program at a time, but keep copies** of each application and the documents you send.
- **Online** – most counties have an online portal (e.g., **BenefitsCal.com** for CalWORKs, county‑specific portals for GA).
- **In‑person** – visit your local County Social Services Agency.
- **By phone or mail** – follow the instructions on the agency’s website (e.g., Alameda County phone (510) 272‑3663).
3. **Tell each agency about the other benefits** you are receiving or plan to apply for.
- Most applications ask, “Are you receiving any other public assistance?” Answer **yes** and list them.
4. **Complete any required follow‑up** (interviews, verification of income, SAR‑7 reports, etc.).
5. **Keep your benefits active** by reporting changes within the required time frame (usually 10 days for income or household changes).

If you’re having trouble paying rent after losing your job, California offers several **emergency rental‑assistance programs** and other safety‑net services. Most programs can give you a **one‑time cash grant** or a **short‑term loan** to cover overdue rent, utilities, or a security deposit.
## 1. Emergency Rental Assistance (ERA)

You live in California (proof needed – lease, utility bill, driver’s license, etc.)

You can show loss of wages, reduced hours, or unemployment benefits.

column1: > **Note:** Exact income limits and maximum award amounts **vary by county**. Check your county’s website or call 211 for the most current numbers.
### Steps to Apply
1. **Gather needed documents** (see the checklist below).
2. **Find your local ERA program** – start by dialing **211** or visiting your county’s social services page.
3. **Complete the application** – many counties allow online submission; some accept paper forms or phone calls.
4. **Submit supporting documents** (rent ledger, utility bills, proof of income loss).
5. **Wait for decision** – most counties aim to approve within 2–4 weeks.
6. **Receive funds** – the money is usually sent directly to your landlord or utility company, or to you as a voucher.

column1: ## How to Get Started
1. **Apply for Unemployment Insurance (UI)**
- **Where:** <https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/>
- **Steps:**
1. Create an EDD account.
2. Fill out the UI claim (you’ll need your last employer’s name, dates worked, and reason you left).
3. Submit any required documents (e.g., termination letter, final pay stub).
- **When:** Claims are usually processed within 10‑14 days; first payment follows your first **bi‑weekly certification**.
2. **Register on CalJOBS**
- **Where:** <https://edd.ca.gov/en/jobs_and_training/Caljobs/>
- **Why:** Required for UI certification and gives you access to job listings, resume tools, and training alerts.
3. **Visit Your Local AJCC (One‑Stop)**
- **Find one:** <https://www.cdss.ca.gov/inforesources/one-stop-centers>
- **What you’ll get:** Free career counseling, resume help, interview workshops, and referrals to WIOA training or CalWORKs/TANF.
4. **Ask About Training Vouchers (WIOA)**
- Bring your UI claim number and any proof of income (pay stubs, SSI/SSDI statements) to the AJCC.
- If eligible, you may receive a **Vocational Training Voucher** that covers tuition for approved programs.
5. **Apply for Additional Support (CalFresh, Medi‑Cal, LIHEAP)**
- These programs have separate applications but often accept the same proof of income used for UI or CalWORKs.
- Applying early can reduce gaps in food, health, or housing while you job‑search.

[Source 13] I just lost my job - how does that affect my application for CalFresh?
URL: https://www.getcalfresh.org/en/faq

You can definitely apply for CalFresh if you just lost your job. If your income recently stopped, your county will only count any final payments you got in the last 30 days to calculate how much CalFresh you will receive in the first month. If you still have any income, your ongoing benefits will be based only on that income, not income that has stopped. You should provide proof of any money you got in the last 30 days if you can.

It isn't required, but it can be helpful to provide any proof you have that your income has stopped. This could be a letter, or a screenshot of an email or text from your employer that explains that you are no longer working. If you can’t get proof, write a letter that explains that you aren’t working. Make sure to include the last date you worked, and sign and date it.

Q_006,How do I apply for Medi-Cal after a layoff?,"## Getting Medi‑Cal after a layoff
Losing a job can be stressful. Medi‑Cal (California’s Medicaid program) can give you free or low‑cost health coverage while you look for new work. Below is a simple step‑by‑step guide.
### 1. Who can qualify?

column3: **What to check**

After a layoff the county will look at the money you earned in the last 30 days (your final paycheck). If that amount is at or below the Medi‑Cal income limit (about 138 % of the federal poverty level for most adults), you are likely eligible.
Include everyone who lives with you and shares food, bills, or housing.
Must live in California.

• U.S. citizens, permanent residents, refugees, asylees, and certain other qualified non‑citizens can apply.

If you already receive a qualifying public assistance program (e.g., **CalFresh**, **CalWORKs**, **SSI**, **Section 8**, **LIHEAP**, **WIC**) you automatically meet the income test.

Q_007,What are the income limits for Unemployment Insurance?,"## Unemployment Insurance (UI) – Income / Earned‑Wage Requirements

column3: What it means for you

UI does **not** have a single “income limit.”  To qualify you must have earned **enough wages** during the **base period** (the first four of the last five completed calendar quarters before you file).  The exact amount varies, but you generally need at least **$1,300‑$1,500** in total wages (or $900 if you lived in an area with a high unemployment rate).

Once you’re approved, your weekly benefit is **based on your highest‑earning quarter** in the base period.  The state sets a **minimum** (about $40) and a **maximum** (currently $450 per week).  Your exact amount will be calculated by the EDD.

• You must be **unemployed through no fault of your own** (or have had a significant reduction in hours).
• You must be **available for work** and **actively looking for a job** each week you certify.
• If you have any earnings while collecting UI, you must report them each week; they may reduce your benefit for that week.

column1: ### How to find out if you meet the wage requirement
1. **Gather your recent pay stubs, W‑2s, or 1099‑G statements** for the last 12‑18 months.
2. **Log in to UI Online** (myEDD) or call the UI line (1‑800‑300‑5616) and ask for a “base‑period earnings check.”
3. The EDD will tell you whether your wages meet the minimum threshold for your county’s unemployment rate.

column1: ### What Happens When You Lose Your Job?

1. **Gather Your basic info** – your most recent pay stubs, latest tax return (or estimate of annual income), Social Security number, and proof of California residency (driver’s license, utility bill, lease).
2. **Check your household size** – count everyone who lives with you and shares income (spouse, children, other dependents).
3. **Run a quick online screen** – the Covered California “Shop & Compare” tool can tell you instantly if you qualify for Medi‑Cal or for premium subsidies.
4. **Apply** – you can start online, but many counties require a **paper or in‑person** application for Medi‑Cal.
5. **Provide supporting documents** – usually:
* Photo ID (driver’s license, state ID)
* Proof of income (pay stub, unemployment benefits letter, or self‑employment records)
* Proof of residence (lease, utility bill)
* Immigration status documents if you are not a citizen (e.g., green card, work permit)
6. **Timeline** – Most counties give a **decision within 30 days** of a complete application. If additional info is needed, they’ll contact you; try to respond quickly to avoid delays.
### County‑Specific Notes

- **Every California county runs its own Medi‑Cal office** (often called “County Social Services” or “Public Assistance”). The exact forms, office hours, and whether you can upload documents online can differ.
- Some counties (e.g., **Los Angeles, San Diego, Alameda**) have **expedited “Express” Medi‑Cal** for unemployed adults, meaning you can get coverage within a few days after a complete application.
- If you live in a **rural county**, you may need to travel to a nearby city office or request a mailed application.
**Tip:** Call your county’s Medi‑Cal office first to ask about **“express” or “quick‑start” enrollment** for unemployed adults.

1. **Run the Covered California screen** now – it’s free and instant.
2. **Contact your county Medi‑Cal office** (search “Medi‑Cal [County name]”) and ask about “express enrollment for unemployed adults.”
3. **Gather the documents** listed above and fill out the application (online or paper).
4. While you wait for a decision, **apply for CalFresh and UI** – they have short processing times and can give you food assistance and cash while you’re looking for work.
5. If you have medical bills already, call the hospital’s **financial assistance** office right away and mention your job loss; many will start a reduction process while you’re waiting for Medi‑Cal.

**You’re not alone.** Losing a job is stressful, but California has a network of programs designed to keep you and your family healthy and fed. You can start your CalWORKs application **online** **or** by contacting the **social services office** in the county where you live.

## Quick Steps to Apply (Online)
1. **Create a BenefitsCal account** – you’ll need an email address and a password.
2. **Select “CalWORKs”** from the list of programs.
3. **Answer eligibility questions** (household size, income, pregnancy/child status).
4. **Upload required documents** (see list below).
5. **Submit the application**.
6. You’ll get a **confirmation number** and a caseworker may contact you for any missing info.

**Typical processing time:** Usually **2–4 weeks** for a decision. If you need urgent help (e.g., for rent or utilities), ask the caseworker about **emergency/short‑term assistance**, which can be approved within a few days.
## What You’ll Need (Documents)

## Who Can Get CalWORKs?
- **Parents or caretakers** of children **under 18** (or under 19 if a child is a full‑time high‑school student).
- **Pregnant** people.
- Families whose **income and resources** are below the state limits (limits vary by household size and county).
- People **receiving or eligible for other public assistance** (e.g., CalFresh) may also qualify.
> **Note:** Exact eligibility thresholds differ **by county**, so the local office will give you the most accurate numbers.
## After You Apply
1. **Caseworker Review** – They may call to verify information or request more paperwork.
2. **Decision Letter** – You’ll receive a notice that tells you if you’re approved, the benefit amount, and when payments start.
3. **Benefit Delivery** – Payments are usually **deposited directly** into a bank account or a **magnetic debit card** (CalWORKs Card).
4. **Ongoing Requirements** – You’ll need to meet work‑search or training activities (the “W” in CalWORKs) and report any changes in income, address, or family size.

Q_010,What documents do I need for Unemployment Insurance and how do I apply?,"## Unemployment Insurance (UI) – Quick Overview

Unemployment Insurance gives a short‑term cash payment to workers who lost a job (or had hours cut) **through no fault of their own**.  Payments are usually **$40‑$450 a week** and are meant to help you while you look for new work or training.
## Who Can Get UI?  (Basic eligibility)

column3: What it means for you
You earned enough wages during a “base period” (the first 4 of the last 5 quarters before you filed).
You are out of work or only partially working **through no fault of your own**.
You are physically able, available, and actively looking for work each week.
You have a Social Security number and are authorized to work in the U.S. (citizens and most permanent residents qualify).
You must be able to accept suitable work right away.

column1: *If you’re not sure you meet the rules, **apply anyway** – the EDD will tell you if you qualify.*
## Steps to Apply
1. **Gather required documents** (see list below).
2. **Create a myEDD account** – this is the online portal you’ll use for the whole process.
3. **File your UI claim** – online is fastest, but you can also fax, mail, or call.
4. **Register for CalJOBS** – a state job‑search site you’ll need to certify each week.
5. **Certify for benefits** – every two weeks you’ll answer simple questions online (or by phone).
6. **Receive your first payment** – processing usually takes about **3 weeks** after you file.
7. **Continue certifying** until you find work or your benefit period ends.

Losing a job can be stressful, but California has several programs that can give you meals right away while you look for work.

## 1. CalFresh – fast food assistance
### Basic eligibility
- You live in California.
- Your household income is at or below the **gross monthly limit** (about 200 % of the federal poverty level).
- You have **limited resources** (typically less than $2,500 in cash, bank accounts, or assets).
- You are a U.S. citizen, permanent resident, or have another qualifying immigration status.
### Steps to apply

column3: What to do

• Photo ID (driver’s license, state ID, or passport)
• Proof of residence (lease, utility bill, or mailed letter)
• Recent pay stubs, bank statements, or a **termination letter** showing your job ended this month
• Social Security numbers for all household members
Go to **[BenefitsCal.com](https://www.benefitscal.com)** and select “CalFresh”. The online form takes about 15‑20 minutes.
Your county will call (usually within 7‑14 days) for a short eligibility interview. Have the documents ready to upload or fax.
County has **30 days** to approve or deny. If you qualify for expedited service, you may get a **temporary benefit card** in as little as a week.
Benefits are loaded onto an EBT card each month. You can start buying groceries as soon as the card is active.

column1: ### Quick‑help tip

- When you apply, **ask for “expedited CalFresh”**. Tell the clerk you were laid off this month and have no income. Most counties will give you a one‑time emergency voucher (about $100‑$200) while your full case is processed.
## 2. CalWORKs – cash aid that can cover food and more
### Who can apply?
- Families with **children** (or pregnant women) who meet income and resource limits.
- Single adults with a **disability** may also be eligible.
### How to apply

column3: What to do

• ID and proof of residence
• Proof of income loss (termination notice, last pay stub)
• Birth certificates for any children in the household

- **Online** at **[BenefitsCal.com](https://www.benefitscal.com)** (choose “CalWORKs”)
- Or call your **County Social Services Agency** – find the number here: **[CDSS County Contacts](https://www.cdss.ca.gov/calworks/contact-us)**
County staff will schedule a phone or in‑person interview within a week or two.
Within **30 days** you’ll get a written decision. If you need money right away, many counties can give **short‑term emergency cash** (often a $100‑$300 grant) while your full case is pending.
If approved, you’ll receive a monthly cash payment (direct deposit or check) that you can use for food, rent, utilities, clothing, medical care, etc.

column1: ## 3. Unemployment Insurance (UI) – weekly income while you job‑search
### Basic eligibility
- You were **laid off** (no fault of your own) or had a **significant reduction in hours**.
- You earned enough wages during the **base period** (usually the first four of the last five completed quarters).
### How to apply
1. **Gather information** – Social Security number, driver’s license/ID, your most recent employer’s name, address, and dates of employment.
2. **Apply online** – Visit the **[California EDD portal](https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/)** and click “Apply Now”.
3. **Register with CalJOBS** – After you’re approved, you’ll need to create a profile on **[CalJOBS](https://www.caljobs.ca.gov/)** and certify each week you’re looking for work.
4. **First payment** – Expect about **3 weeks** from your initial application to receive the first benefit check or direct deposit.
> **Tip:** You can **apply for UI and CalFresh at the same time**. They don’t affect each other, and UI income will be counted when CalFresh calculates your benefit amount.

column1: ## Basic Eligibility Checklist
You must meet **all** of the following. If you’re not sure, apply – the EDD will tell you what you qualify for.
1. **Social Security number** and legal authorization to work in the U.S.
2. **Earned enough wages** during the base period (the exact amount changes each year).
3. **Totally or partially unemployed** – you have no work or only reduced hours.
4. **Unemployed through no fault of your own** (e.g., lay‑off, reduction of hours, or a good‑cause quit).
5. **Physically able** to work.
6. **Available for work** and **actively looking** for a job each week.
7. **Ready to accept suitable work** immediately.

*Note:* Some details (like “good cause” definitions) can vary **by county** because local labor market offices may have different documentation requirements. Always check with your county’s American Job Center if you get a request for extra proof.

## Tips to Help You Get the Most You’re Eligible for
1. **Apply right away** – There’s no penalty for applying even if you later find out you’re not eligible.

2. **Report every dollar you earn** – The first $25 (or 25 % of wages, whichever is larger) is not deducted, but any amount over that reduces your weekly UI payment. Reporting accurately avoids overpayment notices.
3. **Keep a simple job‑search log** – Save screenshots of job listings, email confirmations, or notes about applications. This makes it easier if the EDD asks for proof.
4. **Use the CalJOBS “Job‑Search Tracker”** – The system automatically records your activity, satisfying the “looking for work” requirement.
5. **Consider training benefits** – If you qualify, you can receive UI while you take approved classes or vocational training, which can raise future earnings.
6. **Stay on top of weekly certifications** – Missing a certification week can pause or end your benefits. Set a reminder on your phone or calendar.

7. **Check county‑specific rules** – Some counties require additional documentation (e.g., proof of transportation for job‑search activities). Call your local **America’s Job Center of California** if you receive a request you don’t understand.

column1: ### Basic Steps to Get Started
1. **Apply for Unemployment** – Do this right away at the EDD website. You’ll need your Social Security number, former employer’s name, and dates of work.
2. **Create a CalJOBS Account** – Register within 21 days of the notice you get from the EDD. Upload a current resume.
3. **Visit Your County Social Services Agency** – Ask about CalWORKs, CalFresh, and any local job‑training or transportation help. Bring:
* Photo ID (driver’s license or state ID)
* Proof of California residence (utility bill, lease)

URL: https://www.getcalfresh.org/en/faq

You can definitely apply for CalFresh if you just lost your job. If your income recently stopped, your county will only count any final payments you got in the last 30 days to calculate how much CalFresh you will receive in the first month. If you still have any income, your ongoing benefits will be based only on that income, not income that has stopped. You should provide proof of any money you got in the last 30 days if you can.

It isn't required, but it can be helpful to provide any proof you have that your income has stopped. This could be a letter, or a screenshot of an email or text from your employer that explains that you are no longer working. If you can’t get proof, write a letter that explains that you aren’t working. Make sure to include the last date you worked, and sign and date it.

I’m sorry you’re going through this. Losing a job and feeling down is tough, but there are a number of resources in California that can give you **financial help, housing stability, mental‑health support, and job‑search assistance**. Below is a quick guide to get you started.
## 1. Immediate Emotional Support

## 2. Unemployment Insurance (UI)
### What It Is
*Temporary cash assistance for people who lost work through no fault of their own.*
### Basic Eligibility

column3: Details
Must be unemployed or working fewer hours than before.
Must be looking for work each week and able to accept suitable work.
Must have earned at least $1,300 total in the “base period” (the first four of the last five completed quarters).
Must be a U.S. citizen, permanent resident, or have a work‑authorised visa.

column1: ### How to Apply
1. **Create an online account** at the California Employment Development Department (EDD) – **[edd.ca.gov/unemployment](https://edd.ca.gov/unemployment/)**.
2. **Complete the UI claim** (about 30 min).
3. **Provide required documents** (most are electronic; you may need pay stubs, last employer’s address, and your Social Security number).
4. **Schedule the required phone interview** (EDD will call you within 2‑4 weeks).
### Timeline
* First payment usually arrives **about 3 weeks** after your claim is approved.
* You must **certify** each week (or every two weeks) that you’re still unemployed and looking for work.
> **Note:** Processing times can vary by *county* because some local EDD offices have higher claim volumes.
## 3. Emergency Housing & Rent Help
### a. 211 – Your One‑Stop Referral
*Dial **211** (or visit [211.org](https://www.211.org/)) to speak with a local specialist.*
They can connect you to:
* **Emergency rental assistance** (may be county‑run or city‑run programs).
* **Shelters or short‑term housing** if you’re at risk of homelessness.
* **Utility payment assistance** (electric, gas, water).
### b. County‑Based Rental Assistance (example)

## 7. Quick Step‑by‑Step Checklist
1. **Talk to someone now** – dial **988** or call **211**.
2. **File for Unemployment Insurance** – create an EDD account and submit your claim.
3. **Call 211** to learn about **emergency rent/utility assistance** in your county.
4. **Locate a HUD housing counselor** (HOPE Hotline) for help with applications.
5. **Apply for health coverage** (Medi‑Cal or Covered California).
6. **Register with CalJOBSSM** and explore training or CTB if you want to study while receiving UI.
7. **Check eligibility for CalWORKs or CalFresh** for additional cash/food help.
## 8. Things to Keep Handy
* Photo ID (driver’s license or state ID)
* Social Security number
* Recent pay stubs or proof of income (bank statements, unemployment claim, etc.)
* Lease or mortgage statement
* Utility bills (if applying for utility assistance)
* Any letters from a landlord or eviction notice (if you have one)
### You’re Not Alone

California has many safety nets, and the first step is often just **making a phone call**. Even if you don’t qualify for one program, the staff can point you to another that might fit your situation. Keep a notebook or a phone note of the names and contact numbers you’re given, and follow up within a few days.
If you ever feel unsafe or have thoughts of harming yourself, **call 988** right away or go to your nearest emergency department (dial **911**).

Q_023,I’m getting a severance and might do part-time gig work. Can I still get unemployment and also Medi-Cal?,"## You can get **Unemployment Insurance (UI)** and **Medi‑Cal** at the same time

Losing a job, getting a severance payment, or doing part‑time gig work does **not** automatically stop you from receiving either benefit. Below is a simple guide to help you understand the basics, what you’ll need, and the next steps.
## 1. How UI and Medi‑Cal work together

column3: Your **gross earnings** from any work (including gig jobs) are reported each week when you certify. A severance payment is counted as **income** for the weeks it covers.
column4: UI benefits are counted as **income**, but the Medi‑Cal income limits are higher than the CalFresh limits, so many people qualify even while receiving UI.

• Lost job through no fault of your own (or reduced hours).

• Meet California residency and citizenship/immigration rules.
• Have household income at or below the program’s limits (varies by family size).
• Must not have other health coverage that pays first.

column3: Receiving UI **does not reduce** your UI benefit amount. It is **separate** from Medi‑Cal eligibility.
column4: Getting UI may **reduce** the amount of Medi‑Cal assistance you qualify for, but you can still get coverage—often at a low cost.

## 2. What to do next
### Step 1 – Apply for Unemployment (UI)
1. **Gather your information**
- Social Security Number (SSN)
- Driver’s license or ID card number
- Last employer’s name, address, and dates of employment
- Most recent pay stub(s) or a copy of your final paycheck
- Details of any severance or lump‑sum payments (you’ll report the weeks the severance covers)
2. **Apply online** at the California Employment Development Department (EDD) portal:
<https://edd.ca.gov/en/unemployment/>
3. **Register for CalJOBS** (required for most claimants) – you’ll receive a link after you submit the UI application.
4. **Certify weekly** (report any gig‑work earnings, severance days, etc.).
5. **Expect a first payment** about **3 weeks** after you file, once the claim is processed.
*Source [Source 7] & [Source 9].*
### Step 2 – Apply for Medi‑Cal
You have two primary options: **through Covered California** (if you also want to see if you qualify for a Marketplace plan) or **directly through your county’s Social Services Agency**.

- When your **UI amount changes** (e.g., you start getting payments or the amount goes up/down) tell your Medi‑Cal caseworker.
- If you **pick up new gig work**, report the earnings each week to the EDD and also to Medi‑Cal when you file your monthly income report.

## 7. Quick checklist to get started
1. **File UI claim** today at the EDD website.
2. **Gather documents** listed above (ID, proof of residence, severance info, gig earnings).
3. **Apply for Medi‑Cal** (Covered California or county office) within the next few weeks.
4. **Register for CalJOBS** and start weekly job searches.
5. **Report any income changes** (UI, gig work, severance) to both UI and Medi‑Cal promptly.
6. **Ask about CalFresh, Lifeline, and other local aid** when you contact your county office.
### You’re not alone

Losing a job is stressful, but California has a network of programs designed to keep you fed, healthy, and connected while you look for your next opportunity. Take one step at a time, keep good records, and reach out to your local Social Services Agency if you need help completing any forms—they’re there to assist you.

## 1. Emergency Rent & Utility Assistance

## 2. Starting Your Unemployment Insurance Claim
### A. Basic Eligibility (California)

## 3. Other Helpful Programs While You Wait
- **California Training Benefits (CTB)** – If you enroll in a state‑approved training program, you can keep UI payments. Check the **[CTB page](https://edd.ca.gov/en/jobs_and_training/CTB.aspx)**.
- **CalWORKs** – Cash assistance for families with children who meet low‑income limits. Contact your county’s Human Services Agency.
- **Medi‑Cal** – Free or low‑cost health coverage; apply at **[Medi‑Cal Online](https://www.coveredca.com)**.

- **California Earned Income Tax Credit (CalEITC)** – May give you a refund when you file taxes next year; you can file early at **[CalFile](https://www.ftb.ca.gov/individuals/file-free-online/calfile.html)**.
- **Local non‑profits & churches** – Many provide “quick cash” or food boxes. 211 can connect you.
## 4. Quick Steps to Take Today
1. **Call 2‑1‑1** (or visit the 211 website) and ask for emergency rental assistance and LIHEAP in *your* county.
2. **Gather the documents** listed above for both the emergency programs and UI.
3. **File your UI claim** online right now at the EDD site.
4. **Notify your landlord** that you’re applying for assistance; many landlords will work with you if they know you’re taking action.
5. **Keep a record** of every phone call (date, name, what was said) and save copies of all applications.
## 5. Remember
- **You are not alone.** Many Californians are in the same situation and there are multiple safety‑net programs ready to help.
- **Do not wait** for the UI payment; emergency assistance can often be approved in a week or less.
- **Do not share personal info** (like your SSN) with anyone who calls you unexpectedly. Only use official government websites or the 211 phone line.

Q_025,I’ve never used benefits. I need help with food and maybe paying for my healthcare. What should I start with in San Francisco County?,"## Getting Started with Food & Health Benefits in **San Francisco County**
You’re not alone—many Californians begin with the same steps. Below is a simple guide to the two main programs that can help you right away, plus other resources you might need.
### 1. **CalFresh** – Food Assistance (SNAP)

column3: Monthly benefits are loaded onto an EBT card that you can use at grocery stores, farmers’ markets, and many online retailers.
Anyone who lives in California, is a U.S. citizen, qualified non‑citizen, or lawfully present immigrant, and meets income & resource limits. (Limits vary by household size.)

1. Go to **[BenefitsCal.com](https://benefitscal.com/)** or **[GetCalFresh.org](https://www.getcalfresh.org/en)**.
2. Create an account and start the **CalFresh** application.
3. You’ll be called by the **San Francisco County Social Services Agency** for a brief interview (usually within 1‑2 weeks).

• Photo ID (driver’s license, state ID, or passport)
• Social Security number (or proof you’re ineligible)
• Proof of residence (utility bill, lease, or mail with your name and address)
• Recent pay stubs, unemployment benefits statement, or other income documents
• Bank statements (if you have a checking/savings account)
**Application → Phone interview (within 7‑14 days) → Decision (usually within 30 days).** If approved, the EBT card arrives in 7‑10 days.

• **CalFresh Helpline:** 1‑877‑847‑3663
• **San Francisco County Social Services Office** (phone 415‑252‑7141)
• In‑person at the **Office of Supportive Services**, 651 Oak St., San Francisco, 2nd Floor.
Some counties require an extra “income verification” step, but the process is similar across California.

column1: ### 2. **Medi‑Cal** – Free or Low‑Cost Health Coverage

column3: Health insurance for low‑income Californians. It covers doctor visits, hospital care, prescription drugs, and more.
Residents of California who meet income limits (generally up to 138 % of the Federal Poverty Level for full coverage) and are U.S. citizens, qualified non‑citizens, or lawfully present immigrants.

1. Visit **[CoveredCA.com](https://www.coveredca.com/support/ombuds-office/)** or **[BenefitsCal.com](https://benefitscal.com/)** and choose **Medi‑Cal**.
2. Complete the online application (you can also call the **Medi‑Cal Helpline**).
3. A county worker may contact you for additional documents.

• Same ID and residence proof as CalFresh
• Income proof (pay stubs, unemployment, SSI, etc.)
• Recent tax return or **IRS Form 4506‑T** (if you file taxes)
• Immigration documents (if you’re a non‑citizen)
**Application → Review (usually 15‑30 days) → Notice of eligibility.** If approved, you’ll receive a **Medi‑Cal Benefits Identification Card (BIC)** in the mail.

• **Medi‑Cal Helpline:** 800‑541‑5555
• **San Francisco County Department of Public Health – Medi‑Cal Office** (phone 415‑514‑3333)
• In‑person at the **San Francisco County Health Services** office, 1100‑weight (check local address).
If you need immediate medical care while your application is pending, ask the county worker about **Emergency Medi‑Cal** or **Interim Assistance**.

column3: Why it matters

column2: **You can apply right now** – most counties start a review within 1‑2 weeks after you submit your online application.
column3: Faster help means you’ll get a **conditional benefit** (money that may be paid before the full interview is finished).

column2: **Unemployment Insurance (UI) and severance are counted as income**.
column3: The amount you receive from UI will be added to your household income when the county calculates your CalFresh benefit. If you haven’t started receiving UI yet, you can still apply and add the amount later.

column2: **Moving to another county in California** – you must re‑apply in the new county. Benefits generally stop when you leave the state.
column3: Your new county will look at the same income information, including UI, so be ready to share the same documents.

column2: **Kids help** – each child adds a “household member” amount, which raises the benefit you can receive.
column3: More children usually means a larger monthly food benefit.

column1: ### How UI Income Affects CalFresh

column3: How it’s counted
UI is treated as **regular monthly income**. The county adds it to any other earnings you have.

column2: **You have applied for UI but haven’t received money yet**
column3: You can still apply for CalFresh. When UI starts, you must **report the new income** to your county (you can upload a screenshot or a benefits letter).
Severance is also counted as income, but it may be spread out over several months in the county’s calculation. Include the amount and the date you received it.
When UI ends, tell the county right away so your CalFresh benefit can be recalculated (often it will go up).

column1: ### Steps to Get CalFresh Quickly
1. **Apply online** at **[BenefitsCal.com](https://www.getcalfresh.org/en)** (the site will send you to the county’s portal).
2. **Upload proof of income**:
* Last 30‑day UI statement or screenshot of your UI account.
* Severance letter or payment record, if you got one.
* Any other earnings (part‑time work, gig income).
* Proof of identity (driver’s license, state ID, or birth certificate).
* Proof of residence (utility bill or lease).
3. **Submit the application** – the county will call you within **1‑2 weeks** for a short eligibility interview (phone interview).
4. **Conditional benefits** – if you need food right away, ask the interviewer about receiving a **conditional issuance** (money paid before the interview is fully completed).

5. **Keep the interview appointment** – if you need to reschedule a phone interview, you can do it online in the *Appointments* section of UI Online (or the county’s portal). In‑person interviews usually can’t be moved.
6. **Report any changes** (new UI amount, loss of job, moving) as soon as they happen. You can upload updates through the same portal or call your county’s CalFresh office.
### Documents to Have Ready

column1: ### If You Move to Your Mom’s Home

column3: What to do
Call the CalFresh office in the new county **within 5 days** of moving and start a new application. Bring the same documents listed above.
California CalFresh ends as soon as you leave the state. You’ll need to apply for the food‑assistance program in the new state (often called SNAP).

column2: **Household size changes** (you and your kids now live with Mom)
column3: The household may become larger (if Mom also gets benefits) or smaller (if she doesn’t). The county will recalculate the benefit based on the new total income and members.
Tell the county if your housing costs go down – it may affect the *housing assistance* portion of other programs you might qualify for.

* **211** – dial **211** or visit **[211.org](https://www.211.org)** to get a list of nearby agencies that can help with CalFresh, rental aid, utilities, and more.

## Quick Checklist Before You Call or Apply
1. **Gather all income proof** (UI, severance, any part‑time work).
2. **Write a short letter** if you can’t get a formal proof of job loss (include last work date, reason for layoff, signature).
3. **Make a list of household members** (you, each child, any other adults).
4. **Have a current address and phone number** where the county can reach you.
5. **Know the date you plan to move** – if it’s soon, tell the county now so they can guide you on the best time to re‑apply.
### You’re Not Alone

Losing a job is stressful, especially with kids to care for. California has many safety‑net programs, and you can start the **CalFresh** application right away while you finish your UI claim. Keep copies of every document you upload, report income changes promptly, and reach out to your local county office if you have any questions—they’re there to help you through each step.

[Source 16] I just lost my job - how does that affect my application for CalFresh?
URL: https://www.getcalfresh.org/en/faq

You can definitely apply for CalFresh if you just lost your job. If your income recently stopped, your county will only count any final payments you got in the last 30 days to calculate how much CalFresh you will receive in the first month. If you still have any income, your ongoing benefits will be based only on that income, not income that has stopped. You should provide proof of any money you got in the last 30 days if you can.

It isn't required, but it can be helpful to provide any proof you have that your income has stopped. This could be a letter, or a screenshot of an email or text from your employer that explains that you are no longer working. If you can’t get proof, write a letter that explains that you aren’t working. Make sure to include the last date you worked, and sign and date it.
